summary.title: Incident Response Patterns: What we have learned at PagerDuty
summary.one_liner: Learn how PagerDuty handled incident response over several years, including MTTR trends, the tools it used, and a postmortem template covering timeline, impact, follow-ups, and communications.
keywords: how to run an incident postmortem
takeaways: MTTR for PagerDuty's largest 25 customers was tracked from 2010 to 2015, with values falling from about 14.7 hours to about 2.1 hours.
PagerDuty used many monitoring and alerting tools, including DataDog, SumoLogic, Wormly, New Relic, Crashlytics, and in-house scripts.
A postmortem should cover an overview, root cause and resolution, customer impact, responders, timeline, what went well and what did not, follow-up tasks, and internal and external communication.
Customer impact should be stated in measurable terms, for example the share of customers who could not log in.
summary.summary: This is a slide deck from a talk given at Agile Conf 2015 by PagerDuty staff, hosted on Speaker Deck. It shares charts of mean time to resolution (MTTR) from 2010 to 2015 for the largest 25 customers and for smaller customers, and it lists the monitoring tools the team used. The deck ends with a postmortem outline: overview, root cause and resolution, customer impact, responders, timeline, retrospective notes, follow-up tasks, and internal and external communication. The page text is sparse, so the chart values are read from slide labels and the deck gives little explanation of the patterns behind them.
